world.bio: Thirty-four years as an ICU nurse at St Vincent's, retired two years ago. Bought two small apartments in Bondi in the early nineties with my late husband when it was still a bit rough; now they're my superannuation and my headache. I run them as short stays through the usual platforms. I swim with the dawn group at Icebergs, volunteer at a hospice on Wednesdays, and spoil two grandsons.
skills_assets: Two one-bedroom apartments in Bondi, one on Campbell Parade side street, one near the Icebergs
Superhost standing and 4.9 average rating across both listings
Thirty-four years of clinical experience in intensive care
Linen and supplies storage in a locked cupboard in the building
A reliable set of keys, smart locks and an online calendar
Ocean swim group of about fifteen at dawn, many of them retirees
Volunteer role at a Waverley hospice

projects.name: Short-stay management
projects.text: Two apartments, roughly 24 guest turnovers a month in season. Each turnover needs cleaning, fresh linen, restocking and a quick check of appliances. The cleaner who did them for five years, Dina, moved to Brisbane in August. I've been doing the Saturday ones myself.

projects.name: Grandsons' school fundraiser
projects.text: Running the cake stall at the Bondi Public School spring fair, 17 October. Need 150 cupcakes and a banner. Recruiting fellow grandparents.

projects.name: Hospice volunteer rota
projects.text: Wednesday afternoons, sit with patients, help families with tea. I started after retirement because I missed the ward.

notes.text: Swim at 5:40. Water 17 degrees. A seal had been hanging around Icebergs and everyone was whispering about it. I did my 600 metres and the cold felt like being slapped by a friend.
Dina phoned from Brisbane, her new job in aged care is good, she sounds happy. I'm happy for her. I'm also staring at a Saturday with two turnovers and no cleaner.
Did the Saturday turnovers myself. Eleven to four. Stripped beds, mopped, did laundry in the building's shared machine. By 3 pm my lower back was like a plank. Dr. Chen would tell me off.
Tried the booking site's recommended cleaners. One cancelled twice. One left a stain on a duvet. One asked for $65 an hour. Compared with Dina who charged $45 and cared.

Second Saturday in a row. Back gave out around 2:30 and I had to sit on the stairs for ten minutes. A guest, a young German woman, noticed and offered to carry my linen. Mortified. Gave her a free night credit.
Grandson Max lost a tooth. Called me to say he'd hidden it under the pillow and the tooth fairy better be 'serious'. Sent $5 via his mum. Max says he is rich.
Volunteered at the hospice. A patient, Mr. Hale, asked me to read the cricket scores. The match was nothing. He sat and listened like it was the last Ashes. We both knew.

Looked at my numbers. Two apartments bring in about $9,200 a month gross in season, but expenses, rates and repairs take almost a third. If I can't keep the cleaning steady the rating will slip and so will the bookings.
Rain. Stayed in. Made lemon curd for the fair. Wrote a list: banner, 150 cupcakes, a volunteer to hand out raffle tickets, a cleaner. The last item hasn't got a line through it.

messages.text: Sophie: Mum, did you really clean both apartments on your own? Maggie: Just Saturday. Sophie: You're 63. Maggie: And fine. Sophie: You pulled your back. Maggie: A little. Sophie: Mum!
Dina: How are the apartments? Maggie: Fine. Dina: Did you find someone? Maggie: Not yet. Dina: I could give you my old sheet-folding trick. Maggie: I'd rather have you back.
Barbara: Tomorrow 5:30? Maggie: Yes. Barbara: Seal's back. Maggie: Is it friendly? Barbara: It's a seal.
Guest: Thanks for the apartment! It was spotless. Maggie: Thank you, glad you enjoyed it. Guest: Please tell the cleaner she's wonderful. Maggie: I will. (I was the cleaner.)
Manager: Reminder that guest turnovers on Saturdays must stay under 10 pm noise limit. Maggie: Of course. Manager: And no hanging towels on the balcony. Maggie: I'll tell guests.

constraints: Back injury limits lifting to about 5 kg
Cannot run turnovers on consecutive Saturdays alone
Building rules ban cleaning noise after 6 pm
Will not use platform cleaners she cannot vet
sensitive: Anxious about running out of money if the rating drops, as the rentals are her main retirement income
Her late husband's illness drained savings
Worried she is getting too old to do her own turnovers
